## Homepage headline

Mac app: lightweight, lives in your menu bar

**Talk to your screen. Zerro does the work.**

Record your screen, explain what you want, and get it done faster.

14-day free trial. No card or Zerro account. Bring your own provider API key.

---

## What is Zerro?

Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar utility that turns a screen recording and spoken
instructions into exactly what you need: an agent prompt, a ready-to-send message,
a code or spreadsheet snippet, a written-up document, or a clear answer when you
just want to understand something. You frame a region of your screen, dictate what
you want in plain language, and Zerro returns ready-to-use text. Paste it into
Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, or any tool that takes text, or send it to a person.

Zerro is open source and bring-your-own-key. Processing is local-first: your Mac
prepares the recording, transcribes your narration (locally by default, or
directly with OpenAI on your own key), and redacts detected secrets. It then
sends the prepared frames and transcript straight to the AI provider you chose,
on your own OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic key, stored in the macOS Keychain. Zerro
never receives recordings, frames, audio, transcripts, prompts, or results; there
are no Zerro servers in the middle and no account required.

Think of it as voice dictation that can see your screen: instead of raw transcribed
text, you get the artifact that fits what you asked for. There's no new app to
learn; the whole flow runs from the menu bar.

---

## How it works: Record. Speak. Done.

1. **Select a region.** Hit the hotkey, drag to frame the part of your screen you
   want Zerro to see. Native macOS crosshair, no window switching.
2. **Dictate what you want.** Talk it through like you'd explain it to a teammate.
   Point at things, change your mind, ramble. Zerro records up to 3 minutes.
3. **Your Mac preps it, then AI.** The recording is prepared and transcribed on
   your machine, with detected on-screen secrets masked. Then a single API call
   on your own key sends the frames and transcript to your provider, which turns
   them into the artifact you asked for.
4. **Paste it anywhere.** The result lands on your clipboard (an agent prompt, a
   ready-to-send message, a snippet, a document, or a plain-language answer),
   ready to drop into Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, or any tool that takes text, or
   to send to a person.

You get the artifact that fits what you asked for, not a raw transcript: agent
prompts arrive as structured Markdown with clear sections (such as Context,
Current State, and Request).

---

## The difference: stop typing it, just say it

Today, getting your screen's context to an AI means screenshotting a few parts of
your screen, pasting them into ChatGPT or your coding agent, and typing out, in
detail, what you want. Writing that description out is the slow, tedious part.

With Zerro, you present your screen instead: hit a hotkey, frame the region, and
talk through what you want out loud. Zerro turns it into exactly what you need (a
prompt, message, snippet, doc, or answer), ready to paste wherever it goes. Same
context, a fraction of the effort.

---

## Built right: native, local-first, no surprises

Zerro is built the way you'd build it if it were your tool.

- **Native Swift & SwiftUI.** A real menu-bar app, built on ScreenCaptureKit. Not
  an Electron tab pretending to be a Mac app.
- **Local-first processing.** Your Mac prepares the recording, transcribes it, and
  redacts detected secrets before anything leaves. The frames and transcript then
  go straight to your AI provider on your own key. No Zerro servers.
- **Bring your own key.** Zerro is bring-your-own-key only. Your OpenAI, Gemini &
  Anthropic keys live in the macOS Keychain, and every generation request goes
  straight from your Mac to your provider on your key, never through Zerro's
  servers.
- **Cost-bounded by design.** A 3-minute hard cap on every recording keeps each
  request fast, cheap, and predictable.
- **Signed & notarized.** The official build ships as a code-signed, notarized
  .dmg, so Gatekeeper will not complain. The source is open under
  GPL-3.0-or-later if you'd rather build it yourself.
- **Sparkle auto-updates.** Updates ship through Sparkle, the standard for indie
  Mac apps. You stay current without thinking about it.

---

## The shift: now we're talking

The keyboard was never the point; it was just the only interface we had. As agents
get better at acting on what you actually mean, typing out every instruction by hand
starts to feel like the bottleneck it always was.

You think faster than you type. You talk faster than you think. Voice closes that
gap, and dictation is becoming the default. You speak nearly 4× faster than you
type. Zerro is built for that future: less typing, more talking.

## FAQ

**What is Zerro?**
Zerro is a native macOS menu-bar app that records a region of your screen and your
voice, then returns exactly what you need: an agent prompt, a ready-to-send message,
a code snippet, a written-up document, or simply a clear answer when you just want
to understand something. Paste it into any AI tool, or send it to a person.

**What can Zerro create?**
From a single recording, Zerro returns the artifact that fits what you asked for:
an agent prompt to hand your AI coding agent, a ready-to-send message, an exact
code or spreadsheet snippet, or a written-up document. It picks the right type from
what you say, so you copy something that's ready to use, not raw transcribed text.
And when you just want to understand something rather than produce an artifact,
Zerro answers your question in plain language instead.

**Can Zerro just explain something or answer a question?**
Yes. You don't have to be making an artifact. Point Zerro at a confusing screen, an
error, a chart, or a contract clause, ask your question out loud, and it answers in
plain language: no prompt, message, or document required. It's just as happy
explaining what you're looking at as it is producing something to paste.

**Which AI tools does Zerro work with?**
Any of them. Zerro puts ready-to-use text on your clipboard, so it works with
ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Perplexity, or any tool that takes text. And when
the artifact is a message or document, it's just as ready to send to a person. It
isn't tied to a single app.

**Do I need to be a developer to use Zerro?**
No. If you can show your screen and say what you want, you can use Zerro. It's just
as useful for drafting a message, grabbing a spreadsheet formula, or writing up
notes as it is for coding. Plenty of people never touch a coding agent at all. They
have Zerro turn a confusing screen into a plain-language document, draft a message,
or pull out the exact snippet they need, no code involved.

**Is there a free trial?**
Yes. The first time an official build runs on a Mac it begins a 14-day free trial,
and reinstalling doesn't reset it. No card and no Zerro account are needed; you add
your own OpenAI, Gemini, or Anthropic API key and use everything Zerro does, and
your provider bills you for the usage as it always does.

**How much does Zerro cost?**
After the 14-day free trial, a Zerro license is $39 one time. It activates on up to
2 Macs at once and includes every Zerro 1.x.x update; a future 2.0 major release
may be sold separately. There is no subscription, no credit balance, and no Zerro
account. You bring your own API keys and pay your AI provider directly for usage.

**Do I need my own API keys?**
Yes. Zerro is bring-your-own-key: add one, two, or all three OpenAI, Gemini, and
Anthropic keys, stored securely in the macOS Keychain, and choose from 5 models
(Claude, GPT & Gemini). Local transcription needs no extra key; optional OpenAI
transcription uses your OpenAI key.

**Is Zerro open source?**
Yes. Zerro is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later, official builds included, so
you can read it, change it, build it yourself, and redistribute it under that
license, and a build you make yourself needs no Zerro license. The $39 pays for
SmartScale's official signed and notarized distribution, its 1.x.x update service,
and support; it doesn't buy or limit any GPL right. The Zerro name and logo are
trademarks covered by a separate trademark policy.

**Is my data private?**
Processing starts on your Mac: the recording is prepared, your narration is
transcribed, and best-effort secret redaction runs before anything leaves. Your Mac
then sends the prepared screen frames and the transcript straight to the AI
provider you chose (OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic) on your own key; your audio stays
on your Mac with local transcription, or goes directly to OpenAI on your OpenAI key
if you choose OpenAI transcription. Zerro has no server in that path and never
receives your recordings, frames, audio, transcripts, prompts, or results.
Redaction is best-effort and covers detected on-screen text, not what you say.

**Does Zerro need an account?**
No. Zerro doesn't require a Zerro account. The trial, your API keys, your license
key, and the local activation credentials are stored on your Mac. Lemon Squeezy
processes the purchase and keeps the purchase, activation, and device records it
needs to run your license.

**How long can a recording be?**
Each recording is capped at 3 minutes. The hard cap keeps every request fast, cheap,
and predictable.
